are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

- **Owner, 2026-10-29:** "start with the extension for now". Handoff here; request.md holds the defaults.
- **Worktree:** `~/devel/framejob-lane-a`, branch `lane-a` from main 9a77cad. main = origin = publish = 9a77cad (v0.3.20 published).

a3e97f9 README: the new video link, and a table of code and test lines per language
title:	Import a .fjgraphic package into a project's graphics
state:	OPEN
author:	kpgalligan
labels:	ai-drafted, low-priority
comments:	0
assignees:	
projects:	
milestone:	
number:	384
--
Spec §11 G-46 added Export… to the Graphic dialog (Insert ▸ Graphic…) and `export_graphic`, which write a `.fjgraphic` package. Nothing reads one back yet; G-46 deferred import to this issue.

What an import needs, from the format as built (`core/src/graphic_package.rs`, G-46 (c)):
- **Where the reader goes:** a reader beside the writer in the core, an `rc_*` export, and its wrapper in `ReelCore.swift`.
- **Checks before writing anything:** stored entries only, `manifest.json` first, `"fjgraphic": 1`, and each file's size and SHA-256 matched against the manifest. A package that fails is refused by name.
- **Names:** each file goes back under its manifest `name` (the project's original name), not its in-package path, so `asset(name)` and the module's `font-family` still resolve.
- **Clashes:** a module, font or asset name already in the project needs a rule. One option is G-23 (c)'s suffixes for fonts and assets, and asking first for the module; another is refusing. Record the choice as a §11 decision.
- **Doors:**
  - File ▸ Import Graphic… and/or From File… in the Graphic dialog accepting `.fjgraphic`.
  - Opening a `.fjgraphic` from Finder: the UTI `com.kgalligan.framejob-graphic` is export-only today, so this would need a document type or an open handler.
  - An MCP mirror (`import_graphic`).
- **Proof:** round-trip E1/E6's packages (`tools/proof/graphic_browser_proof.py`) into a fresh project and compare `render_graphic` frames byte for byte.

  `ctx.height / 1080` in landscape and keeps a portrait (1080 × 1920)
  frame from drawing at 1.78 times the size.
  (b) **Title-safe at every frame.** Everything a template draws, at
  every frame, lies inside the 90 % title-safe rectangle
  (x ∈ [0.05W, 0.95W), y ∈ [0.05H, 0.95H)), at 1920 × 1080, at
  1080 × 1920 and at 1080 × 1080 (the square social canvas, which takes
  the landscape layout). An entrance is a spring, a clipPath wipe or a
  fade, never a move in from off-frame. Long user text is fitted or
  wrapped to stay inside, never kept out by narrowing the schema.
  (c) **A card's background is static.** A full-frame template (one that
  passes `background` to `svg`) draws the same background at frame 0 as at
  every later frame; its outro fades or moves the content only.
  (d) **The faces.** Montserrat 800/900 for text, IBM Plex Mono 500 for
  ticking digits, and `'Source Sans 3'` 600 only for window-frame's UI
  text. Bundled faces only (G-6).
  (e) **Glyphs.** A keycap symbol, a bell, a heart, a play triangle or a
  platform glyph is a generic vector shape drawn by the module; no brand's
  artwork.
  (f) **Accent and outro.** Every template has an `accent` colour prop and
  an outro in about its last 15 frames, keyed to `ctx.durationInFrames`,
  that leaves its last frame bare: clear for an overlay, the background
  alone for a card.

  `graphic/tests/graphics/` except `common::FIXTURES` (road map 10's six,
  which keep their own look and pins) to (b), (c) and (f)'s bare last
  frame at all three sizes, with its defaults, with every combination of
  its `enum` options, and with long text (every `string` property given a
  realistic long value: about 40 characters for a title or label, about
  120 for a quote, ticker or subtitle, a list's longest plausible entries;
  `tests/templates/long_text.rs` names one for each, and a string it does
  not name fails): every sampled frame equals frame 0 outside
  title-safe, and frame 0 has one alpha value there; no warning from `svg`
  or `rasterize`, no `NaN` or `Infinity` in the SVG, with defaults and with
  degenerate data (one point, an all-zero series, `max ≤ min`); and
  `project.yml`'s "Copy Graphic Templates" lists exactly the folder's
  `*.js` files.

- **G-45 — Insert ▸ Graphic… is a dialog: categories, the graphics of
  one, and a looping preview; a template declares its category and a
  one-line description** (owner, 2026-10-29: a graphic browser in place of
  the Insert ▸ Graphic submenu; phase 1 of 2, `.fjgraphic` export being
  the second). Amends G-16.
  (a) **A module's category** is `meta.category` when it is a string that
  is not empty after trimming (trimmed), else "Other".
  (b) **Every bundled template declares one** of Data & Time,
  Screencast, Social & YouTube and Titles & Text, and a one-line
  `meta.description` of at most 120 characters, held by
  `graphic/tests/template_meta.rs` to (c)'s table.
  (c) **The table.** Data & Time: bar-chart, counter, countdown,
  donut-chart, gauge, line-chart, progress-bar. Screencast:
  arrow-highlight, callout, keyboard-keys, step-badge, window-frame.
  Titles & Text: chapter-card, kinetic-type, logo-reveal, lower-third,
  news-ticker, quote-card, title-card. Social & YouTube: end-screen,
  handle-tag, social-popup, subscribe-button.
  (d) **The list.** This Project first, and only when the package's
  `graphics/` holds a module: every project module, whatever its own
  category. Then the templates' categories by case-insensitive name, Other
  last. Within a category the graphics go by title case-insensitively,
  then by name. `list_graphics` answers the same order.
  (e) **The title** is `meta.name` when it is a non-empty string, else the
  stem's title (`lower-third` → "Lower Third"). A This Project graphic whose
  title equals another This Project graphic's, case-insensitively, is shown
  as "<title> — <module name>", in the dialog and in `list_graphics` alike,
  so two copies of one template can be told apart. The templates are now
  COMPILED to read their `meta`, once per process, against the bundled
  fonts; the menu bar still compiles nothing (chrome probes instantiate
  `AppDelegate()`).
  (f) **The door** is Insert ▸ Graphic…, a sheet (the submenu and its From
  File… item are gone; From File… is the sheet's bottom-left button, and
  its open panel follows once the sheet is down). Insert is G-16's act for
  a template: the module written under a free name (G-16 (b)), then one
  clip. For a This Project graphic it places a clip drawn by that module
  and writes no copy. Either is one undo step "Insert Graphic". A module
  that does not compile places nothing, and its sentence is
  "graphics/<name>.js does not compile: <the first diagnostic> (line N)" — in the
  dialog's message line, which stays up, or, for From File…, in a sheet
  (G-16 (c)'s "was written but" is gone, since a This Project graphic was
  not written). The agent's mirror is `list_graphics` and
  `insert_graphic {name, from}`.

- **G-46 — The Graphic dialog's Export… writes a `.fjgraphic` package:
  a stored zip of a manifest, the module, and only the project fonts and
  assets the engine saw it use; never a bundled font** (owner,
  2026-10-29; phase 2 of 2 of the graphic browser).
  (a) **The door.** Export… sits at the sheet's far left, with From
  File… to its right. It is enabled when a graphic is chosen and
  compiles. It opens an `NSSavePanel` as a sheet on the browser, named
  `<module>.fjgraphic`. The browser stays up; the result or the refusal
  goes in `graphicbrowser.message`. Exporting is no edit and no undo
  step.
  (b) **The usage rule.** A fresh library is built: the bundled faces,
  then the project's fonts, then its assets, and the module is compiled
  against it. Each frame is drawn (svg, then rasterize at the meta size,
  else the canvas) with default props: every frame up to 900, and past
  that 900 evenly spaced frames. Then the variants are drawn, one at a
  time with every other prop at its default: each `enum` option other
  than the default, and each boolean's opposite, in schema order, at most
  32, over 30 evenly spaced frames each. Every project font blob and asset
  the engine selected, measured, fell back to or resolved is packed; a
  bundled face never is. A frame that throws is skipped and counted.
  String and asset props are sampled only at their defaults. Accepted: a
  font or asset a module reaches only through a caller's own text or an
  asset prop's non-default value is not packed.
  (c) **The format.** A zip, stored (method 0), version needed 10,
  made-by `0x031E`, flag bit 11 (UTF-8 names), DOS time 0 and date
  `0x0021` (1980-01-01) so the bytes are deterministic, no extra fields,
  no directory entries, external attributes `0o100644 << 16`; no Zip64,
  so an archive over `u32::MAX` bytes is refused. `manifest.json` comes
  first, then `<module>.js`, then the fonts and assets, then the central
  directory. Its paths mirror `graphics/` (`fonts/<n>`, `assets/<n>`), so
  a later import is a copy. The manifest is pretty JSON with a trailing
  newline, in the key order `fjgraphic` (1), `module`, `title`,
  `category`, `description` (string or null), `app_version`, `files`
  (`path`, `name`, `size`, `sha256` each); `path` is the in-package path,
  `name` the file's name in its project folder, `sha256` lowercase hex;
  the manifest does not list itself. **A project font or asset whose name
  the package path cannot hold** (`\`, `:`, a control character, a
  leading `.`) **is never refused at export**: a legal in-package `<n>` is
  non-empty, at most 255 bytes, does not begin with `.`, and holds no
  `/`, `\`, `:` or control scalar (U+0000–U+001F, U+007F–U+009F). For
  `fonts/` and `assets/`, each on its own, the legal names are claimed
  first in the order given; then each illegal one, in order, has each run
  of `\`, `:` or control scalars made one `-` and its leading `.`s
  dropped (an empty result is `file`), and a name already claimed takes
  `-2`, `-3`, … before its last `.` (G-23 (c)'s form), the stem cut by
  whole scalars to stay within 255 bytes. `a:b.ttf` → `fonts/a-b.ttf`;
  `red\dot.png` → `assets/red-dot.png`; `a:b.ttf` beside a legal
  `a-b.ttf` → `fonts/a-b-2.ttf`. The manifest's `name` keeps the
  project's, so an import can restore it and `asset(name)` still
  resolves; a font is found by family, never by file name, so its renamed
  entry changes no picture. The core (`rc_graphic_package_write`) writes
  the archive and answers the manifest; Swift writes `.<file>.partial`
  beside the destination and moves it into place, replacing a file
  already there.
  (d) **The UTI** `com.kgalligan.framejob-graphic` ("Frame Job Graphic",
  conforming to `public.zip-archive` and `public.data`, extension
  `fjgraphic`) is exported only; the app does not open a `.fjgraphic`.
  (e) **`export_graphic {name, from, path}`** is the agent's mirror. It
  runs off main, like `render_graphic`, has no `scope`, and refuses
  `from` and an unknown name as `insert_graphic` does and a module that
  does not compile with (f) of G-45's sentence; a refusal writes nothing.
  It is ask-first in the assistant under AI-7's own criterion: it writes
  a file where the model chose.
  (f) **Import is not built.** It is filed as an issue when the phase
  closes.

content.content:
- **G-16 — Insert ▸ Graphic: where the clip goes, what the module is
  called, and what a module that does not compile does** (road map 10
  §10.9 G5b, 2026-09-25). Insert ▸ Graphic is `write_graphic` of a template
  or a chosen `.js`, then `add_graphic_clip` at the module's `meta`
  duration and size, as ONE undo step "Insert Graphic" (the file write is
  not undoable, G-3).
  (a) **Placement is Add Text's** (`addGeneratedClip`, §4.1 "at the
  playhead"): the front track if the clip fits there, else a new track
  above everything. So no track, or a playhead over a clip, never disables
  the item; it validates on the document's graphics store alone.
  (b) **The name is the file's stem made a module name, then made free**:
  lowercased, every run of anything but `a-z0-9` one `-`, trimmed, at most
  63 (`graphic` when nothing is left) — `My Counter (v2).js` is
  `my-counter-v2` — then `GraphicStore.uniqueModuleName`: the name when
  the folder holds no module of it, else `-2`, `-3`, …, so an insert never
  overwrites a module another clip draws. Duplicate as New Graphic…'s
  suggestion uses the same rule.
  (c) **A module that does not compile stays on disk and places nothing**:
  the person reads "graphics/<name>.js was written but does not compile:
  <the first diagnostic> (line N)" in a sheet, and can fix the file where
  it is.
- **G-17 — An export's Cancel only sets flags; a reader is cancelled only
- **G-23 — An asset's name is one `asset(name)` can use; a bad one is
  renamed as it is copied in and skipped by the scan; a font file unchanged
  on disk is not read again** (issue #105, 2026-10-02).
  (a) **A legal asset name** is non-empty, at most 247 UTF-8 bytes (APFS's
  255 less the `.partial` that `GraphicStore.land(at:writing:)` writes
  first), does not start with `.` or `#`, and holds no `/ : " ' < > &` and
  no control scalar (U+0000–U+001F, U+007F–U+009F). Why: a leading `.` is
  hidden from the scan, a leading `#` is an internal href to usvg, `data:`
  routes to the data resolver, and `asset()` returns a known name unescaped
  (`stdlib.js`), so a quote, `&` or `<` breaks the SVG.
  (b) **Legalising** splits the name at its last `.`; in the stem it drops
  leading characters that are `.`, `#` or forbidden and trailing forbidden
  ones, and replaces each interior run of forbidden characters with one
  `-`; an empty stem becomes `image`; the stem is cut by whole scalars to
  fit 247 bytes. `#logo&mark.png` → `logo-mark.png`.
  (c) **A renamed copy never replaces**: when the legal name is held (by
  the scan or on disk) it takes `-2`, `-3`, … (the stem's tail cut by whole
  scalars so the name stays within 247 bytes). A name that needed no
  renaming keeps the replace it always had. An empty name and a name
  holding `/` stay refused.
  (d) **Both doors rename and say the name used**: `import_graphic_asset`
  answers `name` (the name used) and `renamed_from` (the name asked for,
  only when they differ); File ▸ Add Image to Graphics… shows an
  informational sheet, "\"<from>\" was added as \"<to>\": asset(name)
  cannot use the name it had."
  (e) **The scan skips an illegal visible asset file** with the warning
  `graphics/assets/<file> is not an asset name (no leading . or #; no / :
  " ' < > & or control character; at most 247 bytes) and was skipped`.
  Hidden files stay silent, as before; a 248–255-byte name on disk is now
  skipped and warned.
  (f) **A font file's verdict is reused** while its size, modification
  date and file number are unchanged: it is not read or validated again.
  Accepted: a rewrite that keeps all three is not seen until one changes.
- **G-24 — A graphic's warnings show where its other messages do** (issue
- **G-27 — Deleting a graphic is refused while a clip draws it; the deleted
  text is kept, and that kept text is what marks the name as deleted**
  (issue #103, 2026-10-04, issue batch B84).
  (a) **The tool and the menu item.** `delete_graphic {name}`; File ▸
  Delete Graphic… is its menu item (G-30), one small sheet with a pop-up
  of the project's graphics, over the same body
  (`ProjectDocument.deleteGraphic(named:)`).
  (b) **Used is refused, saying which clips**: `The graphic "<name>" is
  still drawn by <where>; delete those clips or point them at another
  module (set_graphic {name}) first`. `<where>` is one group per
  container, the timeline first then nests by id, joined by " and "; a
  group is `clip 4`, `clips 4 and 9` or `clips 4, 9 and 12`, ids
  ascending, then ` on the timeline` or ` in nest <id>`. The sentence is
  the app's, not a core rule's: it names a file act's precondition.
  (c) **Not the Trash.** `graphics/<name>.js` leaves the folder and its
  bytes are kept with the module's other kept revisions (G-29), so
  `restore_graphic` brings it back. The Trash is somewhere an agent cannot
  reach and a proof would litter. Removing a module for good is deleting
  its folder under `graphics/history/` in Finder.
  (d) **Fonts and assets are left alone**: other modules share them.
  (e) **Not an undo step, never dirty** (G-3). The answer's `note` says so.
  (f) **A file-less name that has kept revisions is a DELETED module.** A
  rename carries its history away with it (G-28 (d)) and a delete always
  leaves the deleted text, so "no file, and something kept" is what a
  deleted name looks like — and, of everything the app FINISHES, only a
  deleted name. A rename killed part-way can leave the same state (G-28
  (f)). G-28 (e)'s repair reads that test and stands aside.
  **Risk accepted:** Undo can bring back a clip whose module was deleted
  after the clip was (delete the clip, delete the module, Undo). That clip
  shows the error card (G-8) until the module is restored by hand; no
  other module is ever moved onto the deleted one's name to fill the gap,
  even one it was once renamed from. The alternative, restoring the file
  on Undo, would make a file write an undo step, which G-3 refuses.
- **G-28 — Renaming a graphic moves the file, its kept revisions and every
  clip that names it; Undo renames the file back** (issue #103,
  2026-10-04, issue batch B84).
  (a) **The tool and the menu item.** `rename_graphic {name, to}`; File ▸
  Rename Graphic… is its menu item (G-30), over the same body
  (`ProjectDocument.renameGraphic(named:to:apply:)`).
  (b) **What moves.** `graphics/<name>.js` becomes `graphics/<to>.js`,
  `graphics/history/<name>/` is folded into `graphics/history/<to>/`, and
  every clip that names the module — on the timeline and inside every
  nest — is repointed by `set_graphic {name}` with no schema, as ONE undo
  step called "Rename Graphic". The project is marked edited only when
  clips changed. No core op was added: the op count stays 59.
  (c) **Refusals, in this order.** The module is absent: `No module named
  "<name>" in graphics/ — the folder holds: <list>`. `to` is not a module
  name: the core's own sentence (`GraphicStore.nameSentence`). **`to` is
  in use by a file** (the scan or the disk, `to == name` included):
  `graphics/<to>.js already exists`. **`to` has no file but a clip already
  names it** (a clip left behind by a deleted module): `The name "<to>" is
  already drawn by <where>; delete those clips or point them at another
  module (set_graphic {name}) first`, `<where>` as in G-27 (b) —
  otherwise that clip would silently start drawing the renamed module and
  Undo could not put things back. A nest is open: `rename_graphic has no
  meaning inside nest <id>: it renames the module for every clip in the
  project, the timeline's included. set_scope with no arguments comes back
  out; then rename.`
  (d) **The kept revisions follow the name**, and `graphics/history/<name>/`
  is gone afterwards. A rename that RETURNS is all-or-nothing: a failure
  part-way leaves the file, the history and the journal where they were —
  a rename refused after its pair was written puts `renames.json` back as
  it was read (its bytes, or no file), so a refused rename journals no
  pair, and an earlier pair of the same two names is still there for Undo.
  That holds for both refusals that come after the pair: the history that
  cannot be folded, and the CLIPS that refuse the new name (the edit
  throws, or leaves a clip behind) — there the file and its history are
  moved back under `<name>` and the journal is put back as it was read
  before the rename; a failed move back leaves the file at `<to>` and the
  pair, so (e)'s repair can make it. One thing the clips' arm cannot put
  back: a rename onto a DELETED module's name (the risk accepted below)
  has folded the two histories before the clips are asked, so the move
  back carries the deleted module's kept texts under `<name>` and leaves
  nothing kept under `<to>` (store probe H18 measures each of these).
  A crash between its steps is not a failure the app can put back: (f).
  The journal pair of (e) is written, and read back, after the file moves
  and BEFORE the history is folded (a fold cannot be undone): **a rename
  that could not be journalled is refused** — `graphics/<name>.js could
  not be renamed: its rename could not be journalled in
  graphics/history/renames.json` — so no rename succeeds that Undo could
  not repair.
  (e) **What Undo does.** The file rename itself is not an undo step
  (G-3), but the clips' names are model state. So the store journals each
  rename as a pair `[a, b]` in `graphics/history/renames.json` (at most
  32, oldest first, a repeated unordered pair moved to the end): the app
  moved the file FROM `a` TO `b`. After every committed project change,
  and once when the store starts, the document REPAIRS, **in one
  direction only**: for each pair, newest first, when the pair's FIRST
  name is drawn by a clip, has no file and has no kept revision, while its
  SECOND name has a file and no clip, the file (and its history) is moved
  back under the first. That move journals the pair the other way round,
  so Redo is the same repair. Undo therefore renames the file back with
  the clips, Redo forward again, a chain of renames undoes and redoes step
  by step, and a project opened after a crash between a FINISHED rename
  and a save is healed (a crash inside the rename is (f)'s). A clip never
  names a module a finished rename took away.
  (Amended by B84's review, 2026-10-04: the repair first tried BOTH
  directions of a pair, which moved a live module under a name whose file
  had been removed outside the app and — once `history/<name>/` was
  removed in Finder, as G-27 (c) tells a person to — under a deleted
  module's name.)
  (f) **What the repair skips, and its limits.** A file-less name WITH
  kept revisions is a deleted module (G-27 (f)): its clips keep the error
  card and no live module is moved under its name. A drawn name with no
  file at a pair's SECOND name is a removal the app did not make — the
  app's own moves leave the file there — and nothing is moved under it. A
  rename made outside the app (Finder, a shell `mv`) writes no journal
  pair and is not repaired, a `mv` back to a pair's first name included.
  **Three limits.** The first: the store cannot see a removal made
  outside the app (nothing is kept for one, G-29 (c)), so with the pair
  `[a, b]`, clips that name `a` with no file and nothing kept for a reason
  OTHER than Undo — repointed onto a new `a.js` that was then removed
  outside the app — cannot be told from an Undo, and `b.js`, when no clip
  draws it, is moved under `a`. The other two are a crash INSIDE a rename
  `<from>` → `<to>`, whose three steps — the file moves, the pair is
  journalled, the history is folded — are not one act on disk. Killed
  after the file moved and before the pair was written, there is no pair:
  `<to>.js` is on disk, the clips name `<from>`, and nothing is repaired
  (a rename made outside the app leaves the same). Killed after the pair
  was written and before the fold finished, the repair heals it when
  `<from>` had nothing kept, and does NOT when it had:
  `history/<from>/` is still there, so `<from>` reads as a deleted module
  (G-27 (f)), its clips keep the error card, and a default
  `restore_graphic {name: <from>}` writes an OLDER text while the current
  one sits undrawn at `<to>.js` (store probe H15 builds that state and
  runs the restore in it). That state cannot be told from a rename
  followed by a new `<from>` written and deleted — the same pair, kept
  texts under `<from>`, an undrawn `<to>.js` — and no order of the three
  steps closes both windows; telling them apart needs a marker on disk
  this decision does not have. The way out of either, by hand:
  `set_graphic {name: <to>}` on the clips.
  (g) **The nest limit.** Rename is refused while a nest is open (the
  menu item is greyed there, G-30 (f)). An unscoped op is re-addressed to the
  open nest (`ProjectDocument.addressed`), so the timeline's clips cannot
  be reached from inside one; making it work there needs a document-level
  core op, which is a larger change and is not built.
  **Risk accepted:** the alternative to (e), a rename that empties the
  undo history, is not safe in this app (`removeAllActions` on a document
  is the "do not flush" pitfall). The repair's cost is one journal read
  per committed change in which some drawn name has no file, and none
  otherwise. **A rename onto the name of a DELETED module** (no file, no
  clip, kept revisions) is none of (c)'s refusals: the two histories fold
  under `to` ((b)), the deleted module's texts as the oldest, and the
  prune past 10 (G-29 (b)) removes those first — a renamed module that

  renamed as it is copied in and skipped by the scan; a font file unchanged
  on disk is not read again** (issue #105, 2026-10-02).
  (a) **A legal asset name** is non-empty, at most 247 UTF-8 bytes (APFS's
  255 less the `.partial` that `GraphicStore.land(at:writing:)` writes
  first), does not start with `.` or `#`, and holds no `/ : " ' < > &` and
  no control scalar (U+0000–U+001F, U+007F–U+009F). Why: a leading `.` is
  hidden from the scan, a leading `#` is an internal href to usvg, `data:`
  routes to the data resolver, and `asset()` returns a known name unescaped
  (`stdlib.js`), so a quote, `&` or `<` breaks the SVG.
  (b) **Legalising** splits the name at its last `.`; in the stem it drops
  leading characters that are `.`, `#` or forbidden and trailing forbidden
  ones, and replaces each interior run of forbidden characters with one
  `-`; an empty stem becomes `image`; the stem is cut by whole scalars to
  fit 247 bytes. `#logo&mark.png` → `logo-mark.png`.

  the scan or on disk) it takes `-2`, `-3`, … (the stem's tail cut by whole
  scalars so the name stays within 247 bytes). A name that needed no
  renaming keeps the replace it always had. An empty name and a name
  holding `/` stay refused.

  item's without the "…"; under it a hint ((c)), a `Graphic:` pop-up of
  the project's graphics, Cancel, and a button reading Rename, Delete or
  Restore. Rename adds a `New name:` field, filled with the chosen
  graphic's name, and the footnote `lowercase letters, digits and -`; its
  button is dimmed until the name is filled in and differs from the
  chosen one. Restore adds one line under the pop-up, `1 version kept` or
  `<n> versions kept`, and lists no version: it restores the newest
  (G-29 (d)), and there is no history browser. Rename and Delete list the
  folder's modules by name. Restore lists every name that has a kept
  text, a deleted module (G-27 (f)) reading `<name> (deleted)` — which is
  how a delete is taken back.
  (c) **The hints, word for word.** Rename: `Every clip that uses the
  graphic follows its new name, on the timeline and inside nests. Undo
  renames it back when a clip uses it; a graphic no clip uses is renamed
  back by renaming it again.` Delete: `A graphic that clips still use
  cannot be deleted. Its code is kept with its earlier versions, so
  Restore Graphic Version… brings it back. Deleting is not an Undo step.`
  Restore: `Puts back the newest kept version of the graphic's code. If
  the graphic has code now, that code is kept in its place, so restoring
  again returns to where you were. Restoring is not an Undo step.` They
  promise only what holds: a rename of a graphic no clip uses makes no
  edit (G-28 (b)) and so no undo step, and a restored DELETED graphic
  replaced nothing, so nothing is kept in its place.
  (d) **Where a sheet opens.** Rename and Restore open on the graphic of
  the selected clip when exactly one clip is selected and its graphic is
  a row — a deleted one included, which is how a clip showing the error
  card gets its code back; otherwise on the first row by name. Delete
  always opens on the first: a selected clip's graphic is in use and
  could not be deleted.
  (e) **A refusal shows in the sheet, which stays up.** The body's
  sentence is shown word for word, with a beep, in a label at the foot of
  the sheet's content, so the person can fix the name or pick another
  graphic; no alert sheet is put up. It is the sentence an agent reads,
  the hint `(set_graphic {name})` included (the owner's choice,
  2026-10-04). The sheet owns two guards, both about the CALL (D2-1): a
  new name that is empty or unchanged (the dimmed button), and an item
  with nothing to list ((f)). The name goes to the body as typed, neither
  trimmed nor lowercased. **There is no second confirmation**: the
  sheet's Delete button is the confirmation, because the code is kept and
  Restore brings it back (G-27 (c)). After a success the sheet closes and
  says nothing; a restored text that does not compile shows the error
  card as any broken graphic does (G-8).
  (f) **When an item is greyed.** Rename and Delete in a project whose
  folder holds no module; Restore when no name has a kept text; Rename
  also while a nest is open (G-28 (g)); all three before the document's
  graphics store exists, and while a sheet is attached.
  (g) **One implementation.** Each act is one call of the body the tool
  calls — `ProjectDocument.renameGraphic(named:to:apply:)`, its `apply`
  the document's `performGroupedEdit("Rename Graphic", …)`,
  `deleteGraphic(named:)`, `restoreGraphic(named:revision:)` with no
  revision — and the sheet reaches no store writer, no op and no undo
  registration of its own.
  **Risk accepted:** a person reads a tool's hint in a refusal. A second
  wording for people would be a second spelling of every sentence to keep
  in step with the first.

content.content:
name: FrameJob
options:
  bundleIdPrefix: com.kgalligan
  deploymentTarget:
    macOS: "26.0"
  createIntermediateGroups: true

# Distribution is Release without FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS (spec §11 V-1): `make dist`
# builds it and checks the binary; Debug and Release carry the dev tools.
configs:
  Debug: debug
  Release: release
  Distribution: release

# Sparkle 2, the published build's updater (spec §11 PUB-6..PUB-9). xcodegen
# links a package per target, not per configuration, so Sparkle.framework is
# embedded in every configuration but loaded only in Distribution (PUB-7):
# Debug and Release drop its load command (`-dead_strip_dylibs` below); only
# Distribution compiles code that uses it (FRAMEJOB_UPDATER below) and holds a
# feed and a key. The first build fetches the package over the network.
packages:
  Sparkle:
    url: https://github.com/sparkle-project/Sparkle
    exactVersion: "2.10.1"

targets:
  FrameJob:
    type: application
    platform: macOS
    sources:
      - path: app/Sources
      - path: app/Assets.xcassets
      - path: app/Resources/Fonts
        type: folder
        buildPhase: resources
      - path: app/Resources/Models
        type: folder
        buildPhase: resources
      # A one-frame 16x16 black movie. A timeline of nothing but text, shapes
      # and images owns no composition track, and AVFoundation gives a
      # composition of empty edits a duration of ZERO — so nothing renders
      # offline. This is the minimum real content that gives such a project a
      # track to tick against; the compositor never samples it.
      - path: app/Resources/Blank.mp4
        buildPhase: resources
      # 10 s of ALAC digital silence, 48 kHz stereo (spec §11 #336). An audio
      # track whose every clip has no source is nothing but empty edits, which
      # an export cannot read; this fills it back to back with real silence.
      - path: app/Resources/Silence.caf
        buildPhase: resources
      - path: app/Resources/Shaders
        buildPhase: sources
    # Sparkle (spec §11 PUB-7): embedded in every configuration, loaded only
    # in Distribution.
    dependencies:
      - package: Sparkle
    settings:
      base:
        PRODUCT_NAME: "Frame Job"
        # The module NSDocumentClass names, the same in every configuration: a
        # PRODUCT_NAME with a space would derive Frame_Job (spec §11 NM-3).
        PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME: FrameJob
        # The Rust core is built for the host arch only; for a universal app,
        # cargo-build both targets and lipo them, then widen this.
        ARCHS: arm64
        SWIFT_VERSION: "5.0"
        ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME: AppIcon
        SWIFT_OBJC_BRIDGING_HEADER: app/Bridging/FrameJob-Bridging-Header.h
        LIBRARY_SEARCH_PATHS:
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/core/target/release
        # The bundled encoders (spec §11 CX-4, CX-5): their headers for the
        # bridging header, and their two static archives linked by full path
        # (never -l, so no codec dylib can ever be picked instead) in this list
        # and in Debug's and Release's, which replace it; Distribution inherits it.
        HEADER_SEARCH_PATHS:
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/build/codecs/include
        OTHER_LDFLAGS:
          - -lframejob_core
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/build/codecs/lib/libSvtAv1Enc.a
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/build/codecs/lib/libvpx.a
        MTL_LANGUAGE_REVISION: UseDeploymentTarget
        ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING: "NO"
        ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME: "YES"
        CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY: "-"
        CODE_SIGN_STYLE: Manual
        DEVELOPMENT_TEAM: ""
        MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET: "26.0"
        # The base version lives in VERSION (spec §11 PUB-2), as Rasterize's
        # does; `make project` exports it as RC_BASE_VERSION (a bare `xcodegen
        # generate` leaves it blank). Local builds read "0.2 (0)"; the publish
        # workflow overrides both settings with "<base>.<run number>" and the
        # run number.
        MARKETING_VERSION: ${RC_BASE_VERSION}
        CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION: "0"
      # The dev-tools seam (AgentServer+DevTools.swift) compiles only under this
      # condition; `$(inherited)` keeps the project-level DEBUG in Debug.
      configs:
        Debug:
          SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS: "$(inherited) FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS"
          # Sparkle is never loaded here (spec §11 PUB-7): no Debug code
          # references it, so the linker drops its load command. Loaded, dyld
          # refuses an ad-hoc framework under the hardened runtime's library
          # validation ("different Team IDs") and the app cannot launch. A
          # per-config OTHER_LDFLAGS replaces the base one, so the core is
          # restated, and so are the encoders' archives (CX-4).
          OTHER_LDFLAGS:
            - -lframejob_core
            - $(PROJECT_DIR)/build/codecs/lib/libSvtAv1Enc.a
            - $(PROJECT_DIR)/build/codecs/lib/libvpx.a
            - -Xlinker
            - -dead_strip_dylibs
          # Xcode 26 splits a Debug executable into a stub and __preview.dylib,
          # and Write Agent Catalog's `codesign -s - -f "$exe"` fails on the split.
          ENABLE_DEBUG_DYLIB: "NO"
          # The Debug build is its own app (spec §11 V-5, NM-3): "Frame Job
          # Debug", its own bundle id and defaults domain, and an Alternate
          # `.framejob` handler, so a double-click opens the real Frame Job.
          # Info.plist reads PRODUCT_NAME for both names and the RC_ setting
          # through `:default=`, so Release and Distribution, which take the
          # base PRODUCT_NAME and leave the handler rank unset, keep theirs.
          PRODUCT_NAME: "Frame Job Debug"
          PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.kgalligan.FrameJob.debug
          RC_PROJECT_HANDLER_RANK: Alternate
        Release:
          SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS: "$(inherited) FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS"
          # As Debug's: Sparkle embedded, never loaded (spec §11 PUB-7;
          # tools/proof/dist_check.py D35 holds it). The encoders' archives
          # restated as Debug's are (CX-4).
          OTHER_LDFLAGS:
            - -lframejob_core
            - $(PROJECT_DIR)/build/codecs/lib/libSvtAv1Enc.a
            - $(PROJECT_DIR)/build/codecs/lib/libvpx.a
            - -Xlinker
            - -dead_strip_dylibs
        # Distribution is the build that ships (spec §11 V-1), and notarization
        # refuses the get-task-allow Xcode injects by default, so it is signed
        # with `entitlements` alone (#145, tools/proof/dist_check.py D14).
        Distribution:
          CODE_SIGN_INJECT_BASE_ENTITLEMENTS: "NO"
          # The updater (spec §11 PUB-6..PUB-9) is Distribution's alone:
          # AppDelegate+Updates.swift compiles only under FRAMEJOB_UPDATER, and
          # Info.plist reads the feed and the EdDSA public key through
          # `:default=` (V-5's pattern), so Debug and Release hold neither.
          # The public key is the owner's (PUB-8); until it lands it is empty
          # and dist_check.py's D31 and published_check.py's P20 refuse it.
          SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS: "$(inherited) FRAMEJOB_UPDATER"
          RC_SPARKLE_FEED_URL: https://github.com/kpgalligan/framejob/releases/latest/download/appcast.xml
          RC_SPARKLE_PUBLIC_KEY: "REDACTED"
    info:
      path: app/Info.plist
      properties:
        CFBundleName: "$(PRODUCT_NAME)"
        CFBundleDisplayName: "$(PRODUCT_NAME)"
        CFBundleShortVersionString: $(MARKETING_VERSION)
        CFBundleVersion: $(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)
        LSMinimumSystemVersion: "26.0"
        LSApplicationCategoryType: public.app-category.video
        NSPrincipalClass: NSApplication
        NSHighResolutionCapable: true
        ATSApplicationFontsPath: Fonts
        NSHumanReadableCopyright: ""
        # Sparkle's feed and EdDSA public key (spec §11 PUB-6, PUB-8): set in
        # Distribution alone, empty in Debug and Release (PUB-7). No
        # SUEnableAutomaticChecks and no SUAutomaticallyUpdate: Sparkle's own
        # defaults apply (PUB-9).
        SUFeedURL: "$(RC_SPARKLE_FEED_URL:default=)"
        SUPublicEDKey: "$(RC_SPARKLE_PUBLIC_KEY:default=)"
        # File ▸ New Recording… (road map 3, R1c) — the microphone half of a
        # recording, which speech never needed (the speech engine reads an
        # extracted file). The microphone takes TWO things, and this key is one:
        # NSMicrophoneUsageDescription, or AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess and
        # the first AVCaptureDeviceInput CRASH the app; and under the hardened
        # runtime the entitlement com.apple.security.device.audio-input
        # (`entitlements` below), without which the grant is refused however
        # the person answers the prompt. Screen Recording has neither key nor
        # entitlement: its prompt is triggered by the first capture or by
        # CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess().
        NSMicrophoneUsageDescription:
          Frame Job records the microphone you choose alongside a screen recording, into
          a file of its own beside the movie. Nothing is sent anywhere.
        # The camera half of a recording (camera-recording CR1a, spec §11 CAM-3)
        # takes the same two things as the microphone: this key, without which
        # AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess(for: .video) and the first camera
        # AVCaptureDeviceInput CRASH the app, and the entitlement
        # com.apple.security.device.camera (`entitlements` below). No
        # NSCameraUseContinuityCameraDeviceType: CR0's D2 listed the iPhone's
        # Continuity Camera without it.
        NSCameraUsageDescription:
          Frame Job records the camera you choose, into a file of its own. Nothing is
          sent anywhere.
        UTExportedTypeDeclarations:
          - UTTypeIdentifier: com.kgalligan.framejob-project
            UTTypeDescription: Frame Job Project
            UTTypeConformsTo: [com.apple.package]
            UTTypeTagSpecification:
              public.filename-extension: [framejob]
          # The Graphic dialog's Export… (spec §11 G-46 (d)): exported only, so
          # Finder names it; no CFBundleDocumentTypes row, as the app opens none.
          - UTTypeIdentifier: com.kgalligan.framejob-graphic
            UTTypeDescription: Frame Job Graphic
            UTTypeConformsTo: [public.zip-archive, public.data]
            UTTypeTagSpecification:
              public.filename-extension: [fjgraphic]
        CFBundleDocumentTypes:
          - CFBundleTypeName: Frame Job Project
            LSItemContentTypes: [com.kgalligan.framejob-project]
            CFBundleTypeRole: Editor
            NSDocumentClass: FrameJob.ProjectDocument
            LSTypeIsPackage: true
            LSHandlerRank: "$(RC_PROJECT_HANDLER_RANK:default=Owner)"
          # Opening a media file makes an UNTITLED project sized to it with
          # the file as the first clip (spec 1) — the app is an Alternate
          # handler for each so Open With… works from the Finder.
          - CFBundleTypeName: QuickTime Movie
            LSItemContentTypes: [com.apple.quicktime-movie]
            CFBundleTypeRole: Editor
            NSDocumentClass: FrameJob.ProjectDocument
            LSHandlerRank: Alternate
          - CFBundleTypeName: MPEG-4 Movie
            LSItemContentTypes: [public.mpeg-4, com.apple.m4v-video]
            CFBundleTypeRole: Editor
            NSDocumentClass: FrameJob.ProjectDocument
            LSHandlerRank: Alternate
          - CFBundleTypeName: Movie
            LSItemContentTypes: [public.movie]
            CFBundleTypeRole: Editor
            NSDocumentClass: FrameJob.ProjectDocument
            LSHandlerRank: Alternate
          - CFBundleTypeName: Audio
            LSItemContentTypes:
              [com.apple.m4a-audio, public.mp3, com.microsoft.waveform-audio, public.aiff-audio]
            CFBundleTypeRole: Editor
            NSDocumentClass: FrameJob.ProjectDocument
            LSHandlerRank: Alternate
          - CFBundleTypeName: Image
            LSItemContentTypes: [public.png, public.jpeg, public.heic]
            CFBundleTypeRole: Editor
            NSDocumentClass: FrameJob.ProjectDocument
            LSHandlerRank: Alternate
    # The hardened-runtime entitlement the microphone needs (road map 3, R0's
    # second surprise: a bare swiftc probe never needs it, the signed app
    # does), and the camera's, added on that finding (spec §11 CAM-3: CR0
    # measured only a bare binary under the terminal's grant). The file is
    # GENERATED by xcodegen from these properties, like app/Info.plist, and
    # git-ignored beside it.
    entitlements:
      path: app/FrameJob.entitlements
      properties:
        com.apple.security.device.audio-input: true
        com.apple.security.device.camera: true
    preBuildScripts:
      # The bundled encoders (road map "codec-export" C0, spec §11 CX-5):
      # tools/codecs/build_codecs.py fetches, checks and builds SVT-AV1 and
      # libvpx into build/codecs/, or reuses them by its stamp (a no-op costs
      # well under a second), so the step runs every build. The PATH is Build
      # Rust Core's without cargo; the script also finds cmake in
      # /opt/homebrew/bin or /usr/local/bin when Xcode's PATH lacks Homebrew,
      # and builds under its own scrubbed environment, so this step and a
      # shell's `make codecs` compute one key.
      - name: Build Codecs
        basedOnDependencyAnalysis: false
        script: |
          set -e
          export PATH="/usr/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH"
          python3 "$PROJECT_DIR/tools/codecs/build_codecs.py"
        outputFiles:
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/build/codecs/lib/libSvtAv1Enc.a
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/build/codecs/lib/libvpx.a
      - name: Build Rust Core
        # cargo decides staleness, so the step runs every build (a no-op
        # costs 0.1 s).
        basedOnDependencyAnalysis: false
        script: |
          set -e
          # /usr/bin is ahead of Xcode's own PATH, so `cc` is the xcrun shim a
          # shell finds and not the toolchain's clang: with SDKROOT unset (below) that
          # clang has no SDK, and a COLD build of rquickjs-sys's C stops at
          # "'stdlib.h' file not found". `make app` never met it, because
          # `make rust` builds first; an archive on a fresh checkout does.
          export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:/usr/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH"
          cd "$PROJECT_DIR/core"
          # Xcode exports MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET and SDKROOT, a shell's
          # `make rust` neither, and rquickjs-sys's build script reruns when
          # MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET changes: with them set, the shell build
          # and this step rebuilt rquickjs-sys, graphic and core in turn, and
          # a tree copy's step (its `core` is a symlink) rewrote the tree's
          # core/target (#225). Unset, both builds are the same build.
          env -u MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET -u SDKROOT cargo build --release
        outputFiles:
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/core/target/release/libframejob_core.a
    # The graphics reference (road map 10's G4a): `graphic_reference` reads
    # GraphicsAPI.md, and a package's graphics/ gets both as API.md and
    # API.d.ts. Copied under new names, so not a resources-phase entry.
    postBuildScripts:
      - name: Copy Graphics Reference
        script: |
          set -e
          dest="$TARGET_BUILD_DIR/$UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH"
          mkdir -p "$dest"
          cp "$PROJECT_DIR/docs/graphics-api.md" "$dest/GraphicsAPI.md"
          cp "$PROJECT_DIR/docs/graphics-api.d.ts" "$dest/GraphicsAPI.d.ts"
        inputFiles:
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/docs/graphics-api.md
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/docs/graphics-api.d.ts
        outputFiles:
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicsAPI.md
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicsAPI.d.ts
      # The graphic templates (road map 10's G5b): Insert ▸ Graphic lists the
      # bundled templates of graphic/tests/graphics/, copied as they are.
      - name: Copy Graphic Templates
        script: |
          set -e
          dest="$TARGET_BUILD_DIR/$UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH/GraphicTemplates"

          cp "$PROJECT_DIR"/graphic/tests/graphics/*.js "$dest/"
        inputFiles:

          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/bar-chart.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/callout.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/chapter-card.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/countdown.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/counter.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/donut-chart.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/end-screen.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/gauge.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/handle-tag.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/keyboard-keys.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/kinetic-type.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/line-chart.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/logo-reveal.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/lower-third.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/news-ticker.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/progress-bar.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/quote-card.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/social-popup.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/step-badge.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/subscribe-button.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/title-card.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/window-frame.js
        outputFiles:
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/arrow-highlight.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/bar-chart.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/callout.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/chapter-card.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/countdown.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/counter.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/donut-chart.js

          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/keyboard-keys.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/kinetic-type.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/line-chart.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/logo-reveal.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/lower-third.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/news-ticker.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/progress-bar.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/quote-card.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/social-popup.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/step-badge.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/subscribe-button.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/title-card.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/window-frame.js
      # The encoders' licence and patent texts (spec §11 CX-5 (4), #376):
      # build/codecs/licenses/<library>/ as Build Codecs installed them, into
      # Contents/Resources/Licenses/ (tools/proof/dist_check.py D40/D41).
      - name: Copy Codec Licences
        basedOnDependencyAnalysis: false
        script: |
          set -e
          dest="$TARGET_BUILD_DIR/$UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH/Licenses"
          rm -rf "$dest"
          mkdir -p "$dest"
          cp -R "$PROJECT_DIR"/build/codecs/licenses/* "$dest/"
      # The assistant's agent helper (agent/, spec §11 AI-1): compiled with
      # Bun, placed in Contents/Helpers and signed by agent/build.sh, before
      # Xcode signs the app around it — the app's own signature does not
      # cover a nested executable. Without bun it fails; it never skips.
      - name: Build Agent Helper
        # Bun rebuilds the helper in well under a second, so it runs every build.
        basedOnDependencyAnalysis: false
        script: /bin/sh "$PROJECT_DIR/agent/build.sh" helper
      # The stdio MCP server external clients start (road map 14's MC3, spec
      # §11 MC-3): mcp-proxy/ built by cargo, put in Contents/Helpers beside the
      # assistant's helper and signed as agent/build.sh signs that one (the
      # hardened runtime, no entitlements), before Xcode signs the app.
      - name: Build MCP Proxy
        basedOnDependencyAnalysis: false
        script: |
          set -e
          export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH"
          cd "$PROJECT_DIR/mcp-proxy"
          cargo build --release
          HELPERS="$TARGET_BUILD_DIR/$CONTENTS_FOLDER_PATH/Helpers"
          mkdir -p "$HELPERS"
          cp "$PROJECT_DIR/mcp-proxy/target/release/framejob-mcp" "$HELPERS/"
          IDENTITY="${EXPANDED_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY:--}"
          TIMESTAMP=""
          if [ "$IDENTITY" != "-" ]; then TIMESTAMP="--timestamp"; fi
          codesign --force --options runtime $TIMESTAMP \
            --sign "$IDENTITY" "$HELPERS/framejob-mcp"
      # The third-party notices (#376, spec §11 PUB-10): every shipped crate,
      # npm package, Bun, Sparkle, the encoders, the model and the fonts, into
      # Contents/Resources/Acknowledgements.txt (not Licenses/, which Copy Codec
      # Licences empties). After Build Agent Helper (its `bun install` makes
      # agent/node_modules) and before Write Agent Catalog, which reseals the
      # bundle. Distribution fails on a Bun other than the vendored licence's
      # (--strict-bun); the others note it. tools/proof/dist_check.py D42/D43.
      - name: Write Acknowledgements
        basedOnDependencyAnalysis: false
        script: |
          set -e
          export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$HOME/.bun/bin:$HOME/.local/share/mise/shims:/usr/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH"
          STRICT=""
          if [ "$CONFIGURATION" = Distribution ]; then STRICT="--strict-bun"; fi
          python3 "$PROJECT_DIR/tools/licenses/acknowledgements.py" $STRICT \
            --out "$TARGET_BUILD_DIR/$UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH/Acknowledgements.txt"
      # The catalog snapshot framejob-mcp lists from while no Frame Job runs
      # (MC-4; MC1 q1): the just-linked executable, ad-hoc signed alone in place
      # because the linker leaves it unsigned and arm64 kills an unsigned exec,
      # run with -RCWriteCatalog (AgentCatalogSnapshot.swift), then the bundle
      # signed again as Xcode's CodeSign signs it. It fails on a non-zero exit
      # and on any `Frame Job: ` line, the parity check complaining.
      - name: Write Agent Catalog
        basedOnDependencyAnalysis: false
        script: |
          set -e
          out="$TARGET_BUILD_DIR/$UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH/agent-catalog.json"
          exe="$TARGET_BUILD_DIR/$EXECUTABLE_PATH"
          # The codesign below re-seals the bundle, writing the marker
          # tools/proof/proof_app.py reads as a complete build; any failure
          # from here on removes it, so a failed build is refused (B88).
          marker="$TARGET_BUILD_DIR/$CONTENTS_FOLDER_PATH/_CodeSignature/CodeResources"
          trap 'rm -f "$marker"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$out")"
          codesign -s - -f "$exe"
          rc=0
          output=$("$exe" -RCWriteCatalog "$out" 2>&1) || rc=$?
          if [ -n "$output" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$output"; fi
          if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "error: the catalog writer exited $rc"
            exit 1
          fi
          if printf '%s\n' "$output" | grep -q 'Frame Job: '; then
            echo "error: the catalog writer's output holds the parity check's complaint"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Xcode's CodeSign task does not see this step change the bundle, so
          # a build where nothing else changed skips it and would ship the
          # ad-hoc signature above (no entitlements) over a catalog written
          # after it. Seal the bundle as that task does: its identity and its
          # processed entitlements (B88; a second no-op `make dist` failed D14).
          IDENTITY="${EXPANDED_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY:--}"
          TIMESTAMP="--timestamp=none"
          if [ "$IDENTITY" != "-" ]; then TIMESTAMP="--timestamp"; fi
          RUNTIME=""
          if [ "$ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME" = YES ]; then RUNTIME="-o runtime"; fi
          codesign --force --sign "$IDENTITY" $RUNTIME $TIMESTAMP \
            --entitlements "$TARGET_TEMP_DIR/$FULL_PRODUCT_NAME.xcent" \
            --generate-entitlement-der "$CODESIGNING_FOLDER_PATH"
          trap - EXIT
        inputFiles:
          # Ordering only (the step runs every build): the entitlements it
          # signs with, and the Info.plist its seal covers.
          - $(TARGET_TEMP_DIR)/$(FULL_PRODUCT_NAME).xcent
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(INFOPLIST_PATH)

schemes:
  FrameJob:
    build:
      targets:
        FrameJob: all
    run:
      config: Release
    # Product > Archive never ships the dev tools.
    archive:
      config: Distribution

toolUseResult.stdout:
name: FrameJob
options:
  bundleIdPrefix: com.kgalligan
  deploymentTarget:
    macOS: "26.0"
  createIntermediateGroups: true

# Distribution is Release without FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS (spec §11 V-1): `make dist`
# builds it and checks the binary; Debug and Release carry the dev tools.
configs:
  Debug: debug
  Release: release
  Distribution: release

# Sparkle 2, the published build's updater (spec §11 PUB-6..PUB-9). xcodegen
# links a package per target, not per configuration, so Sparkle.framework is
# embedded in every configuration but loaded only in Distribution (PUB-7):
# Debug and Release drop its load command (`-dead_strip_dylibs` below); only
# Distribution compiles code that uses it (FRAMEJOB_UPDATER below) and holds a
# feed and a key. The first build fetches the package over the network.
packages:
  Sparkle:
    url: https://github.com/sparkle-project/Sparkle
    exactVersion: "2.10.1"

targets:
  FrameJob:
    type: application
    platform: macOS
    sources:
      - path: app/Sources
      - path: app/Assets.xcassets
      - path: app/Resources/Fonts
        type: folder
        buildPhase: resources
      - path: app/Resources/Models
        type: folder
        buildPhase: resources
      # A one-frame 16x16 black movie. A timeline of nothing but text, shapes
      # and images owns no composition track, and AVFoundation gives a
      # composition of empty edits a duration of ZERO — so nothing renders
      # offline. This is the minimum real content that gives such a project a
      # track to tick against; the compositor never samples it.
      - path: app/Resources/Blank.mp4
        buildPhase: resources
      # 10 s of ALAC digital silence, 48 kHz stereo (spec §11 #336). An audio
      # track whose every clip has no source is nothing but empty edits, which
      # an export cannot read; this fills it back to back with real silence.
      - path: app/Resources/Silence.caf
        buildPhase: resources
      - path: app/Resources/Shaders
        buildPhase: sources
    # Sparkle (spec §11 PUB-7): embedded in every configuration, loaded only
    # in Distribution.
    dependencies:
      - package: Sparkle
    settings:
      base:
        PRODUCT_NAME: "Frame Job"
        # The module NSDocumentClass names, the same in every configuration: a
        # PRODUCT_NAME with a space would derive Frame_Job (spec §11 NM-3).
        PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME: FrameJob
        # The Rust core is built for the host arch only; for a universal app,
        # cargo-build both targets and lipo them, then widen this.
        ARCHS: arm64
        SWIFT_VERSION: "5.0"
        ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME: AppIcon
        SWIFT_OBJC_BRIDGING_HEADER: app/Bridging/FrameJob-Bridging-Header.h
        LIBRARY_SEARCH_PATHS:
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/core/target/release
        # The bundled encoders (spec §11 CX-4, CX-5): their headers for the
        # bridging header, and their two static archives linked by full path
        # (never -l, so no codec dylib can ever be picked instead) in this list
        # and in Debug's and Release's, which replace it; Distribution inherits it.
        HEADER_SEARCH_PATHS:
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/build/codecs/include
        OTHER_LDFLAGS:
          - -lframejob_core
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/build/codecs/lib/libSvtAv1Enc.a
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/build/codecs/lib/libvpx.a
        MTL_LANGUAGE_REVISION: UseDeploymentTarget
        ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING: "NO"
        ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME: "YES"
        CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY: "-"
        CODE_SIGN_STYLE: Manual
        DEVELOPMENT_TEAM: ""
        MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET: "26.0"
        # The base version lives in VERSION (spec §11 PUB-2), as Rasterize's
        # does; `make project` exports it as RC_BASE_VERSION (a bare `xcodegen
        # generate` leaves it blank). Local builds read "0.2 (0)"; the publish
        # workflow overrides both settings with "<base>.<run number>" and the
        # run number.
        MARKETING_VERSION: ${RC_BASE_VERSION}
        CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION: "0"
      # The dev-tools seam (AgentServer+DevTools.swift) compiles only under this
      # condition; `$(inherited)` keeps the project-level DEBUG in Debug.
      configs:
        Debug:
          SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS: "$(inherited) FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS"
          # Sparkle is never loaded here (spec §11 PUB-7): no Debug code
          # references it, so the linker drops its load command. Loaded, dyld
          # refuses an ad-hoc framework under the hardened runtime's library
          # validation ("different Team IDs") and the app cannot launch. A
          # per-config OTHER_LDFLAGS replaces the base one, so the core is
          # restated, and so are the encoders' archives (CX-4).
          OTHER_LDFLAGS:
            - -lframejob_core
            - $(PROJECT_DIR)/build/codecs/lib/libSvtAv1Enc.a
            - $(PROJECT_DIR)/build/codecs/lib/libvpx.a
            - -Xlinker
            - -dead_strip_dylibs
          # Xcode 26 splits a Debug executable into a stub and __preview.dylib,
          # and Write Agent Catalog's `codesign -s - -f "$exe"` fails on the split.
          ENABLE_DEBUG_DYLIB: "NO"
          # The Debug build is its own app (spec §11 V-5, NM-3): "Frame Job
          # Debug", its own bundle id and defaults domain, and an Alternate
          # `.framejob` handler, so a double-click opens the real Frame Job.
          # Info.plist reads PRODUCT_NAME for both names and the RC_ setting
          # through `:default=`, so Release and Distribution, which take the
          # base PRODUCT_NAME and leave the handler rank unset, keep theirs.
          PRODUCT_NAME: "Frame Job Debug"
          PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.kgalligan.FrameJob.debug
          RC_PROJECT_HANDLER_RANK: Alternate
        Release:
          SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS: "$(inherited) FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS"
          # As Debug's: Sparkle embedded, never loaded (spec §11 PUB-7;
          # tools/proof/dist_check.py D35 holds it). The encoders' archives
          # restated as Debug's are (CX-4).
          OTHER_LDFLAGS:
            - -lframejob_core
            - $(PROJECT_DIR)/build/codecs/lib/libSvtAv1Enc.a
            - $(PROJECT_DIR)/build/codecs/lib/libvpx.a
            - -Xlinker
            - -dead_strip_dylibs
        # Distribution is the build that ships (spec §11 V-1), and notarization
        # refuses the get-task-allow Xcode injects by default, so it is signed
        # with `entitlements` alone (#145, tools/proof/dist_check.py D14).
        Distribution:
          CODE_SIGN_INJECT_BASE_ENTITLEMENTS: "NO"
          # The updater (spec §11 PUB-6..PUB-9) is Distribution's alone:
          # AppDelegate+Updates.swift compiles only under FRAMEJOB_UPDATER, and
          # Info.plist reads the feed and the EdDSA public key through
          # `:default=` (V-5's pattern), so Debug and Release hold neither.
          # The public key is the owner's (PUB-8); until it lands it is empty
          # and dist_check.py's D31 and published_check.py's P20 refuse it.
          SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS: "$(inherited) FRAMEJOB_UPDATER"
          RC_SPARKLE_FEED_URL: https://github.com/kpgalligan/framejob/releases/latest/download/appcast.xml
          RC_SPARKLE_PUBLIC_KEY: "REDACTED"
    info:
      path: app/Info.plist
      properties:
        CFBundleName: "$(PRODUCT_NAME)"
        CFBundleDisplayName: "$(PRODUCT_NAME)"
        CFBundleShortVersionString: $(MARKETING_VERSION)
        CFBundleVersion: $(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)
        LSMinimumSystemVersion: "26.0"
        LSApplicationCategoryType: public.app-category.video
        NSPrincipalClass: NSApplication
        NSHighResolutionCapable: true
        ATSApplicationFontsPath: Fonts
        NSHumanReadableCopyright: ""
        # Sparkle's feed and EdDSA public key (spec §11 PUB-6, PUB-8): set in
        # Distribution alone, empty in Debug and Release (PUB-7). No
        # SUEnableAutomaticChecks and no SUAutomaticallyUpdate: Sparkle's own
        # defaults apply (PUB-9).
        SUFeedURL: "$(RC_SPARKLE_FEED_URL:default=)"
        SUPublicEDKey: "$(RC_SPARKLE_PUBLIC_KEY:default=)"
        # File ▸ New Recording… (road map 3, R1c) — the microphone half of a
        # recording, which speech never needed (the speech engine reads an
        # extracted file). The microphone takes TWO things, and this key is one:
        # NSMicrophoneUsageDescription, or AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess and
        # the first AVCaptureDeviceInput CRASH the app; and under the hardened
        # runtime the entitlement com.apple.security.device.audio-input
        # (`entitlements` below), without which the grant is refused however
        # the person answers the prompt. Screen Recording has neither key nor
        # entitlement: its prompt is triggered by the first capture or by
        # CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess().
        NSMicrophoneUsageDescription:
          Frame Job records the microphone you choose alongside a screen recording, into
          a file of its own beside the movie. Nothing is sent anywhere.
        # The camera half of a recording (camera-recording CR1a, spec §11 CAM-3)
        # takes the same two things as the microphone: this key, without which
        # AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess(for: .video) and the first camera
        # AVCaptureDeviceInput CRASH the app, and the entitlement
        # com.apple.security.device.camera (`entitlements` below). No
        # NSCameraUseContinuityCameraDeviceType: CR0's D2 listed the iPhone's
        # Continuity Camera without it.
        NSCameraUsageDescription:
          Frame Job records the camera you choose, into a file of its own. Nothing is
          sent anywhere.
        UTExportedTypeDeclarations:
          - UTTypeIdentifier: com.kgalligan.framejob-project
            UTTypeDescription: Frame Job Project
            UTTypeConformsTo: [com.apple.package]
            UTTypeTagSpecification:
              public.filename-extension: [framejob]
          # The Graphic dialog's Export… (spec §11 G-46 (d)): exported only, so
          # Finder names it; no CFBundleDocumentTypes row, as the app opens none.
          - UTTypeIdentifier: com.kgalligan.framejob-graphic
            UTTypeDescription: Frame Job Graphic
            UTTypeConformsTo: [public.zip-archive, public.data]
            UTTypeTagSpecification:
              public.filename-extension: [fjgraphic]
        CFBundleDocumentTypes:
          - CFBundleTypeName: Frame Job Project
            LSItemContentTypes: [com.kgalligan.framejob-project]
            CFBundleTypeRole: Editor
            NSDocumentClass: FrameJob.ProjectDocument
            LSTypeIsPackage: true
            LSHandlerRank: "$(RC_PROJECT_HANDLER_RANK:default=Owner)"
          # Opening a media file makes an UNTITLED project sized to it with
          # the file as the first clip (spec 1) — the app is an Alternate
          # handler for each so Open With… works from the Finder.
          - CFBundleTypeName: QuickTime Movie
            LSItemContentTypes: [com.apple.quicktime-movie]
            CFBundleTypeRole: Editor
            NSDocumentClass: FrameJob.ProjectDocument
            LSHandlerRank: Alternate
          - CFBundleTypeName: MPEG-4 Movie
            LSItemContentTypes: [public.mpeg-4, com.apple.m4v-video]
            CFBundleTypeRole: Editor
            NSDocumentClass: FrameJob.ProjectDocument
            LSHandlerRank: Alternate
          - CFBundleTypeName: Movie
            LSItemContentTypes: [public.movie]
            CFBundleTypeRole: Editor
            NSDocumentClass: FrameJob.ProjectDocument
            LSHandlerRank: Alternate
          - CFBundleTypeName: Audio
            LSItemContentTypes:
              [com.apple.m4a-audio, public.mp3, com.microsoft.waveform-audio, public.aiff-audio]
            CFBundleTypeRole: Editor
            NSDocumentClass: FrameJob.ProjectDocument
            LSHandlerRank: Alternate
          - CFBundleTypeName: Image
            LSItemContentTypes: [public.png, public.jpeg, public.heic]
            CFBundleTypeRole: Editor
            NSDocumentClass: FrameJob.ProjectDocument
            LSHandlerRank: Alternate
    # The hardened-runtime entitlement the microphone needs (road map 3, R0's
    # second surprise: a bare swiftc probe never needs it, the signed app
    # does), and the camera's, added on that finding (spec §11 CAM-3: CR0
    # measured only a bare binary under the terminal's grant). The file is
    # GENERATED by xcodegen from these properties, like app/Info.plist, and
    # git-ignored beside it.
    entitlements:
      path: app/FrameJob.entitlements
      properties:
        com.apple.security.device.audio-input: true
        com.apple.security.device.camera: true
    preBuildScripts:
      # The bundled encoders (road map "codec-export" C0, spec §11 CX-5):
      # tools/codecs/build_codecs.py fetches, checks and builds SVT-AV1 and
      # libvpx into build/codecs/, or reuses them by its stamp (a no-op costs
      # well under a second), so the step runs every build. The PATH is Build
      # Rust Core's without cargo; the script also finds cmake in
      # /opt/homebrew/bin or /usr/local/bin when Xcode's PATH lacks Homebrew,
      # and builds under its own scrubbed environment, so this step and a
      # shell's `make codecs` compute one key.
      - name: Build Codecs
        basedOnDependencyAnalysis: false
        script: |
          set -e
          export PATH="/usr/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH"
          python3 "$PROJECT_DIR/tools/codecs/build_codecs.py"
        outputFiles:
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/build/codecs/lib/libSvtAv1Enc.a
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/build/codecs/lib/libvpx.a
      - name: Build Rust Core
        # cargo decides staleness, so the step runs every build (a no-op
        # costs 0.1 s).
        basedOnDependencyAnalysis: false
        script: |
          set -e
          # /usr/bin is ahead of Xcode's own PATH, so `cc` is the xcrun shim a
          # shell finds and not the toolchain's clang: with SDKROOT unset (below) that
          # clang has no SDK, and a COLD build of rquickjs-sys's C stops at
          # "'stdlib.h' file not found". `make app` never met it, because
          # `make rust` builds first; an archive on a fresh checkout does.
          export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:/usr/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH"
          cd "$PROJECT_DIR/core"
          # Xcode exports MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET and SDKROOT, a shell's
          # `make rust` neither, and rquickjs-sys's build script reruns when
          # MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET changes: with them set, the shell build
          # and this step rebuilt rquickjs-sys, graphic and core in turn, and
          # a tree copy's step (its `core` is a symlink) rewrote the tree's
          # core/target (#225). Unset, both builds are the same build.
          env -u MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET -u SDKROOT cargo build --release
        outputFiles:
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/core/target/release/libframejob_core.a
    # The graphics reference (road map 10's G4a): `graphic_reference` reads
    # GraphicsAPI.md, and a package's graphics/ gets both as API.md and
    # API.d.ts. Copied under new names, so not a resources-phase entry.
    postBuildScripts:
      - name: Copy Graphics Reference
        script: |
          set -e
          dest="$TARGET_BUILD_DIR/$UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH"
          mkdir -p "$dest"
          cp "$PROJECT_DIR/docs/graphics-api.md" "$dest/GraphicsAPI.md"
          cp "$PROJECT_DIR/docs/graphics-api.d.ts" "$dest/GraphicsAPI.d.ts"
        inputFiles:
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/docs/graphics-api.md
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/docs/graphics-api.d.ts
        outputFiles:
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicsAPI.md
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicsAPI.d.ts
      # The graphic templates (road map 10's G5b): Insert ▸ Graphic lists the
      # bundled templates of graphic/tests/graphics/, copied as they are.
      - name: Copy Graphic Templates
        script: |
          set -e
          dest="$TARGET_BUILD_DIR/$UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH/GraphicTemplates"
          mkdir -p "$dest"
          cp "$PROJECT_DIR"/graphic/tests/graphics/*.js "$dest/"
        inputFiles:
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/arrow-highlight.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/bar-chart.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/callout.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/chapter-card.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/countdown.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/counter.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/donut-chart.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/end-screen.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/gauge.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/handle-tag.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/keyboard-keys.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/kinetic-type.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/line-chart.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/logo-reveal.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/lower-third.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/news-ticker.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/progress-bar.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/quote-card.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/social-popup.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/step-badge.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/subscribe-button.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/title-card.js
          - $(PROJECT_DIR)/graphic/tests/graphics/window-frame.js
        outputFiles:
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/arrow-highlight.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/bar-chart.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/callout.js

          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/handle-tag.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/keyboard-keys.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/kinetic-type.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/line-chart.js
          - $(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH)/GraphicTemplates/logo-reveal.js
